goal.objective:
Make audits folder/project-scoped to the current cwd project: the primary audit target is the folder where pi was opened; external code (parent repo, sibling projects, libraries outside cwd) may be READ to diagnose a failure affecting the current project and may be reported as a finding only when it blocks or breaks the current project, but typo/nit fixes in unrelated projects are out of scope and never auto-queued.

Boundaries: no changes to unrelated sibling projects for cosmetic issues; external library findings are DECIDE or FIX only when they affect current project's correctness. Hellhunter example: opening pi in web/games/wip/hellhunter audits hellhunter, not the entire dracon-platform.

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: lets audit the entire entire game and fix what we can, we would also need a ton of auto generated loot taht gets better as we have better loot and enemies that get better as we have better loot. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

(3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". tasks.verificationContract: Add behavioral regressions for recovery-resume, session handoff, and pending-list records dated in the future; run the focused lifecycle/recovery tests and npm run check.

subtasks.title: Verify all freshness validators and their shared semantics
Reject future timestamps without weakening stale/identity fences
Add tests covering all affected sidecar types
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Make tracked transcript tails discoverable
tasks.verificationContract: Add a regression for a matching transcript beyond the current 25-file window; preserve bounded main-thread I/O or document a safer index/lookup; run agents-panel and display tests plus npm run check.

subtasks.title: Confirm the 25-file cap is the actual failure mode
Implement a bounded, identity-safe lookup that does not silently hide tracked children
Add a regression for the older matching transcript
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Route audit fan-out through the selected state root
tasks.verificationContract: Add a sessionDir regression proving list-audit fan-out reads the selected GLLA state root and queues findings; run list-audit, state-root, and release/type checks.

subtasks.title: Trace the runtime root registration and detached fan-out boundary
Use the admitted state-root resolver without weakening generation fences
Add a hermetic sessionDir fan-out test
Check the finding with the resulting commit

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

tasks.title: Reconcile package-store-facing installation docs
tasks.verificationContract: Resolve the docs/INDEX.md versus INSTALL.md symlink-setup mismatch, review README.md for current shipped behavior, and prove README/INSTALL/docs are included in npm pack output; run npm run check.

subtasks.title: Choose source-install wording that matches the supported commands

Run a package dry-run and document release-version/Unreleased status
Check the finding with the resulting commit

tasks.title: Run release gate and final audit review
tasks.verificationContract: Run npm run release:check, inspect all new findings and commits, and obtain a final read-only reviewer report; every new FIX is checked with a real commit and no DECIDE remains unraised.

subtasks.title: Run focused regressions and the full release contract
Re-audit changed boundaries and release/package documentation
Record environment-only failures separately if the gate is blocked
Prepare the six-label completion evidence

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the project before we would commit to to next step and we woudl want to make a release so others are caught up too update teh docs including the one that is visible on pi package store cause thatis the old one so we update our readme then we use that on the store too. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

auditHistory.report:
## Audit

The audit contract is satisfied: four new FIX findings are checked, their commits exist, and no DECIDE findings remain. The release gate also passed.

However, the package-store requirement is not complete. The repository README contains new release guidance, but the published npm/Pi package is still `0.36.1` and does not contain that marker:

```text
--- source marker ---
40:for published versions. The npm/Pi package listing displays this README from
--- registry marker ---
--- registry metadata ---
version = '0.36.1'
dist-tags.latest = '0.36.1'
time.modified = '2026-08-31T00:49:31.797Z'
```

The completion summary itself says publishing is still the next step. Thus the user-facing store README remains stale.

<evidence>
Item: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).
Output:
- [x] FIX: MEDIUM: recovery-resume, session-handoff, and pending-list sidecars accept future-dated timestamps because freshness checks only require `Date.now() - at < window` (`extensions/goal-recovery.ts:63`; `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:796,860,915`) — a future marker can be consumed as fresh and trigger an unexpected resume or replay. Require a non-negative age and add regressions for every sidecar validator. — fixed in 265dafa6 (shared non-negative-age gate + 3 regression tests)

Output:
- [x] FIX: MEDIUM: recovery-resume, session-handoff, and pending-list sidecars accept future-dated timestamps because freshness checks only require `Date.now() - at < window` (`extensions/goal-recovery.ts:63`; `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:796,860,915`) — a future marker can be consumed as fresh and trigger an unexpected resume or replay. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

- Antigravity poll-only inferred 250→1000ms (scripts/durable-wait.mjs)

## Audit report — pi-goal-list-loop-audit v0.38.18 trilogy

**Verdict: work is a partial fix with two tracks re-scoped away from the contract.**

What was checked:
- `tests/mechanical-pipeline.test.ts` (7 tests), `tests/never-streamed-standdown.test.ts` (4), `tests/terminal-completion-notice.test.ts` (2) read in full; targeted `bun test` re-run (9 pass); `tsc --noEmit` clean; `CHANGELOG.md`, `audit/COMPLETION-LIFECYCLE-TRILOGY-2026-09-04.md`, `docs/INDEX.md`/`audit/INDEX.md`, `git tag`, `npm view` inspected.
- Track 1 is real: narrow `cmd 2>&1 | tail/head/grep` pipeline parsed and run shell-free with head-exit semantics; `tee`/redirect/chain refused with no side effects. This matches objective Track 1 ("checker handling pipeline syntax").
- Track 2 does NOT satisfy the objective/contract. Objective demands: "after the user answers ask_user_question, no continuation turn starts — root-cause the dispatch stall, not the aborter." The shipped fix does the opposite: it parks never-streamed turns on first abort (`zombie_auto_retry_refused_never_streamed`, no retry) and rewords the rearm milestone. The regression file contains zero references to `ask_user_question` and no answered-question→continuation-turn behavioral test. Forensics in the audit doc even re-blames the field case to "never streamed, not dispatch."
- Track 3 does NOT satisfy the contract literal. Contract demands "a closed goal clears the waiting-verdict state." The shipped fix sends a fire-once `followUp` `✓ done` notice (`sendTerminalCompletionNotice`) but never clears the `awaiting-verdict` display phase (`goal-loop-display.ts` still returns `awaiting-verdict` for `phase complete` / `pendingCompletion running`). The test pins `pi.sent` growth + source wiring, not state cleared on close.
- Release/docs/publish trail exists (tag `v0.38.18`, `npm view = 0.38.18`, CHANGELOG + audit doc + INDEX entries), but full `release:check` (1912 pass claim) was not reproduced here — only targeted files + `tsc`. Scope: one aspect we would want ot look into is the look and what we are showing and how cuase that is seemingly how our https://pi.dev/packages?name=goal competitors like pi goal x and pi museless harness, not sure about hte top one i think that is just a basic option and fine for that but not our chief competitor, but essentially looks=value least you know better,. Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

(1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

Audit report — pi-goal-list-loop-audit v0.38.23 below-chat GLLA widget redesign

Objective required: forced belowEditor pin, deleted footers, Option-2 single-line glyph-first rows, evidence-age lifesign with breathing head + green→amber→red ramp (color never sole channel), display-only, v0.38.23 ship (bump, changelog, docs, tag).

Checks performed:
- `setWidget("pi-glla", …, { placement: "belowEditor" }` present in `extensions/loops/goal-ui.ts:839`; repo-wide grep for deleted footer strings (`glla agents for full`, `/goal status · /glla`, `/list · /glla`, `more agents · /glla`) returns zero hits under `extensions/` (only historical mentions in CHANGELOG/audit docs).
- Rows in `extensions/goal-agents-panel.ts` are single-line glyph-first (`▶`/`◉`/`⚠`), `silent <bucket>` before suffixes, overflow is count-only (`… N more agents`), `→ objective` header gone, `/glla agents` table untouched (Recent hangs, `└ blocks:` intact).
- Head in `extensions/goal-loop-display.ts` breathes from evidence counters (`headLifesign`), carries `stream <bucket>` as last segment on active-clear heads only, paints head glyph + age + row glyphs by band; meter stays `dim` (progress-colored); no fleet-line code touched.
- `paint = (theme, color, text) => (theme ? theme.fg(color, text) : text)` — undefined theme cannot emit ANSI; lifesign tests render heads + rows with `undefined` theme.
- Reject-class scan: no test file spawns the whole runner (`bun test` appears only as string literals in display.test.ts measureCmd/recent-entry fixtures, never executed).
- Visual audit: no fresh screenshots or image attachments were supplied with the claim, and no native image input path was available in this session — visual evidence is unavailable; verification rests on behavioral pins + source inspection. Verbatim critique for the visual contract item: "no image was provided, so no visual finding is made; widget shape verified via unit pins and source, not via screenshot."

Threshold note (non-blocking): objective parenthetical says "5–20m warning" while code uses `LIFESIGN_STALE_MS = 30m` (warning to 30m, error past it) and head readout emits only the `stream X` label (the `tool edit 2m` example has no distinct label — row evidence rides as a suffix). The verification contract's testable pins (12m → warning frozen ring ◉, hung → error ⚠, fresh → success + readout) are all satisfied; the 20m→30m band is a documented superset in CHANGELOG, not a contradiction of any contract item.

(1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

(1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
objectiveProvenance.originalContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

(1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

(1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

(1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

auditHistory.report:
## Audit report

**Verdict: disapprove.** The shipped work improves clipping and de-imperatives the pending text, but it does not deliver the Codex-style shape the objective requires.

What the objective demands (semantic core): the posted summary opens outcome-first, carries **4–6 bullets where each bullet is one verifiable result with its evidence inline**, closes with **at most one next action plus what was deliberately not done**, and is never truncated mid-word. Pending text states facts, no agent imperatives.

What was actually shipped (v0.38.36):
- `clipSummaryValue` clause-boundary cuts + `buildAuditCountsLine` verdict-only + imperative-free `AUDIT PENDING` — real and verified.
- But the chat summary is still `✓ done — <outcome>` + `Label: value` lines (`Changed:`/`Evidence:`/`Tests:`/…), **not 4–6 verifiable-result bullets**. No bullet character or bullet test exists in the render path.
- The **deliberate non-do is explicitly admitted as not built**: `audit/HUMAN-VOICE-SUMMARY-2026-09-08.md` says "a deliberate-non-do line would require facts we don't store" — i.e. the required "what was deliberately not done" closer is missing by design.
- Tests pin outcome-first, clause cuts, verdict-only counts, and imperative-free pending, but **no test pins bullets, single-next-action, or deliberate non-do** (grep over the three render test files returns zero hits for bullet/deliberate-non-do/single-next-action).
- Visual: no fresh image was supplied in this audit session, so visual evidence is unavailable; the shape gap above is proven from code, not screenshots.

Verification contract item 1 therefore fails on its own terms, and the full-gate log cited by the executor (`/var/tmp/glla-summary-release-check2.log`) tails at 0.38.35, not the claimed 0.38.36 gate — the 0.38.36 full-gate pass is not inspectably proven in the evidence I could read.

<evidence>

- Add the deliberately-not-done fact (store it from the agent claim or durable state — do not ship a "would require facts we don't store" waiver) and pin it with a MockPi test.
- Add MockPi pins for the full shape: bullet count 4–6, each bullet carries inline evidence, single next action, deliberate non-do present, zero mid-word `…` cuts, pending text imperative-free; keep the existing clause-cut and verdict-only pins.
- Re-run the full `TMPDIR=/var/tmp npm run release:check` on v0.38.36+ and cite the fresh log tail showing 0 failures across all files, plus clean `npx tsc --noEmit`.

# Audit report — elapsed-time duplication + PR #47

## Objective check
Cut the `total …` duplication (card showed `active · total 12m 30s` while Bridge tab strip showed `glla: [WORKING] total 12m 30s`): remove timer from Bridge line, keep in card, fold anything missed. GLLA-only unless Bridge line is pi-core-owned. Plus triage PR #47 against current main with re-sync reply and #45/#46-consistent disposition.

## Findings
- Cut is real and correctly attributed: `buildStatusText`/`setStatus("pi-glla",…)` in `extensions/goal-loop-display.ts` + `loops/goal-ui.ts:836` is GLLA-owned; `Chrome Bridge (indefinite)` framing is not. Status branches (idle/busy/working/queued/monitoring) now emit state+counts only; card head (`goalLines` ~:1672) keeps `total` unconditionally. Code comments cite field 20260909_002132.
- Tests pin it: `tests/display.test.ts:83-89` asserts ACTIVE status has no timer; `:170-174` asserts `glla: [WORKING] 3 queued` while card head keeps `total 1m 00s`. `bun test tests/display.test.ts`: 111 pass / 0 fail.
- Full gate log `/var/tmp/glla-elapsed-release-check.log`: 2040 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- PR #47: state CLOSED (2026-09-09), 2 comments. Maintainer reply gives per-piece verdicts (KV-strip real-but-not-portable → byte-stable pointer redesign; auditTasks held; overflow/settings need split PRs), #45/#46-consistent rationale (live `.pi-glla/active.jsonl` blob, 16 ahead/39 behind, bundled features), and merge-based re-sync command. Nothing ported, correctly (nothing was real-and-missing in portable form). `gh pr list` open is empty.
- `audit/ELAPSED-DUPLICATION-PR47-2026-09-09.md` records the cut, verdict, and "nothing was folded because nothing was missing there."
- Visual: no fresh screenshot was attached to this audit payload and no native image input was available in this session, so no fresh visual comparison could be performed — verdict rests on code + render-test pins, not on a screenshot. Verbatim critique: "No fresh UI image was available to inspect; the timer-cut is verified via buildStatusText source and display-test pins (status without total, card head with total), not via a fresh screenshot."

## Outside Scope
None.

Audit report — terminal summary trailer cleanup (v0.38.42)

Objective required: one canonical approval bullet in chat + transcript with no model ID in either (full ID in archive only), via-retry news kept, lone approval folds with verdict count, standalone audit bullet only with news (multiple/disapproved/impossible), machine-path layering unchanged, claim-length stays prompt guidance, shipped as versioned release.

- `buildTerminalApprovalRender` implements `stripApprovalModel` (`auditor <model> approved` → `auditor approved`) applied to shared `chatApproval` used for both `chatLines` and `transcriptLines`; returned `approval` field keeps full input string for archive/persist. - Machine-path layering intact: `chatSafeDetailValue` still strips `/tmp|/var/tmp|*.tgz` only in chat brief; archive path untouched.

## Audit report — GLLA stale-version surfacing (v0.38.44)

**Verdict: approve.**

### Success criteria (from objective)
1. Running GLLA version visible in the UI.
2. Staleness detected against npm latest + nudge.
3. Documented update/reload path.
4. Tests pin version-visibility and staleness.

### Evidence
- `package.json` version `0.38.44`; `npm view pi-goal-list-loop-audit version` → `0.38.44` (live check, exit 0). Registry and repo agree.
- Version tail centralized in `extensions/goal-loop-display.ts:1151-1152`: `buildStatusText()` appends `extras.versionTail` after every per-branch `buildStatusTextBase()` result — inherits to all branches by construction. `extensions/loops/goal-ui.ts:843` always supplies `versionTail: buildVersionTail(runningGllaVersion(), readUpdateCheck(ctx.cwd)?.latest ?? null)`; `runningGllaVersion()` reads `package.json` once (fixed for process lifetime).
- `extensions/glla-update-check.ts`: `buildVersionTail()` → `"· v<running>"` always, plus `"· update v<latest> available"` only when `compareVersions(latest, running) > 0`; `staleUpdateNudge()` returns null for no-cache / current / `unknown`. `refreshUpdateCheck()` throttled by 24h TTL, shells `npm view pi-goal-list-loop-audit version` with 15s timeout, fire-and-forget, never throws, never surfaces failures. `extensions/loops/goal-activation.ts:746` rides the command/lifecycle contact gate.
- `/glla version` (`extensions/glla-version.ts:formatGllaVersion`, routed in `goal-commands.ts:2389`): legacy 3 lines with no cache; with sidecar cache appends `Registry latest: vX.` plus `This session is stale — update: pi install npm:...@latest then /reload.` or `up to date`. Verified by read.
- `INSTALL.md:Updating` section documents status-line form, sidecar `.pi-glla/update-check.json` daily refresh, `pi install npm:pi-goal-list-loop-audit@latest` + `/reload` every session, and `/glla version` staleness check. Quoted verbatim from file.
- Tests: `bun test tests/glla-update-check.test.ts tests/glla-version.test.ts tests/display.test.ts` → 123 pass, 0 fail (reproduced). Covers compare, nudge, tail, cache malformed/future, TTL skip, npm-view cache write, registry-failure no-write; `glla-version.test.ts` pins staleness wording and registration; `display.test.ts:version tail rides the status on every branch` pins tail + nudge suffix. `tsc --noEmit` clean (exit 0). Working tree clean, `git log` shows v0.38.44 tag commit.
- Reject-class check: no test spawns a test runner; only spawn is `npm view ... version` with bounded timeout and depth-capped close handler. No recursion risk.
- Visual contract item: no fresh screenshot or native image input was supplied in this audit session and no external vision provider availability was confirmed, so visual evidence is unavailable rather than invented. Critique verbatim: "No live-session screenshot was available to eyeball; version-tail visibility was instead verified textually — `buildStatusText` with `versionTail` extra renders `[ACTIVE] · v0.38.44` and `update v0.38.44 available` suffix per the display pin, and `goal-ui.ts` supplies the tail on the live render path."

### Outside Scope
None.

<approved/>

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the current project rooted at the cwd where pi was opened (treat any nested .git as a separate project boundary — do not walk into parent or sibling projects). Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix
goal.verificationContract: the audit pass is complete, every new FIX finding has a fix commit and a checked box in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md, and every DECIDE finding has been raised to the user and recorded as DECIDED/DEFERRED (or the report states plainly that none were found).

goal.objective: Run ONE project audit pass and leave the project in a known state. Scope: the current project rooted at the cwd where pi was opened (treat any nested .git as a separate project boundary — do not walk into parent or sibling projects). Primary target is the current project under cwd; external code outside cwd may be READ only to diagnose a failure that blocks the current project, and a finding about external code is valid only when it affects the current project. (1) Run a FRESH audit pass over the codebase — spawn AT LEAST 3 scout subagents in ONE message, one per subsystem, so the survey runs in parallel instead of serial through your own context — each with a TIGHT brief: named directories under cwd, a ~30-40 tool-use budget, and a ~150-line report cap ('if you near the token limit, stop and report what you have') — hunting real problems: bugs, broken flows, regressions, drift between docs and code, dead code, security holes. Not style nits, not speculative refactors. (2) Append every NEW finding to .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md (create the file on the first finding; append-only — never delete, rewrite, or reorder existing lines; never re-report a finding already listed), classified: "- [ ] FIX: SEVERITY: short description (file:line)" for bugs and polish — whether to fix these is NOT a decision — and "- [?] DECIDE: short description (what the choice is, what each side costs)" for direction, trade-offs, and scope questions where two reasonable answers exist. (3) Fix every NEW FIX finding from this pass — real fixes, committed with the repo's configured identity on the current branch (no invented identities or branches) — then check the box: "- [x] … — fixed in <commit>". (4) Change NOTHING for DECIDE findings — RAISE them instead: if any "- [?]" findings exist, present each one to the user with ask_user_question BEFORE calling complete_goal (one question per finding, options from the finding's own two sides plus "Defer"; prose numbered list if ask_user_question is unavailable; Esc = Defer), then record every answer in .pi-glla/audit-loop/findings.md — replace the "- [?]" line with "- [x] DECIDED: <what was chosen> (<date>)" (or "- [x] DEFERRED") so it stops re-surfacing — and queue any chosen work with list_add. (5) Honesty law: never fabricate findings to look busy; never check a box without the fix commit existing; never silently turn a DECIDE into a fix

## Audit report — delegated-session guard spike (goal `20260911115307-u7b6lg`)

**Objective:** `Spike: verify whether GLLA needs pi-goal-x's delegated-session guard, porting only on a positive finding; record the verdict with exact test evidence.`

**Verdict direction is plausible; evidence citation is wrong → disapprove.**

### What checks out
- Guard code exists as claimed: `isWorkerSessionCtx` defined at `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:1574` (`!ctx.hasUI && (mode==="print"||mode==="json")`), enforced at `extensions/loops/goal-activation.ts:1247` (`if (isWorkerSessionCtx(ctx)) return;` before root/restore/owner writes).
- Bounded run reproduces: `bun test` on the 4 cited files → `58 pass, 0 fail` (verified this session).
- Diff is doc-only (survey doc + active.jsonl), consistent with "no port on negative finding".

### Blocking gap: cited "exact test evidence" does not pin the guard
Section 9 correction claims `the guard is pinned by 4 test files` with lines `last-wins:174, stale-self-heal:112, stale-continuation-integration:111, stall-handling:55`. Grep of those files shows:
- `stale-self-heal.test.ts:112` = `SRC.slice(...indexOf("function isForeignCtx"...))` — self-heal ordering assertion, not a worker-admission assertion.
- `stale-continuation-integration.test.ts:111` = a comment (`// Now foreign ctx is different cwd...`).
- `stall-handling.test.ts:55` = `if (isForeignCtx(ctx)) return; noteActivity(true)` — activity gating, not `isWorkerSessionCtx` refusal.
- Only `last-wins.test.ts:174` mentions `isWorkerSessionCtx`, and only for ownership-refresh (`refreshOwnershipStanding`), not `session_start` admission refusal.
- No cited line asserts `goal-activation.ts:1247` refusal. A reader following the citations cannot verify the "no hole" verdict.

The actual direct behavioral pin was omitted: `tests/subagent-host-boundary.test.ts` (4 tests, all pass this session) — `worker cannot be first claimant`, `persistent workers cannot masquerade as silent host successors`, with `workerCtx` (`mode="print"`, `hasUI=false`) refused at `session_start` without mutating state. That is the evidence the verdict needs, and it is uncited.

Secondary: body text still says `Pinned across 7 test files`; the appended correction contradicts it without fixing it.

## Required fixes
- Fix survey §9 body: remove/replace the false `Pinned across 7 test files` sentence so the section is internally consistent.
- Cite the real guard evidence: `tests/subagent-host-boundary.test.ts` (worker-first-claimant, foreign-command, persistent-masquerade tests) with exact test names/lines plus its bounded `bun test` result; keep the 58/0 run only with an accurate characterization (ownership/continuation/stall coverage, not guard pinning) or drop it from the guard claim.
- Re-run and record both bounded runs with exact pass/fail counts after the doc fix.

## Audit report — delegated-session guard spike (goal `20260911115307-u7b6lg`)

**Objective:** `Spike: verify whether GLLA needs pi-goal-x's delegated-session guard, porting only on a positive finding; record the verdict with exact test evidence.`

**Verdict direction is plausible; evidence citation is wrong → disapprove.**

### What checks out
- Guard code exists as claimed: `isWorkerSessionCtx` defined at `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:1574` (`!ctx.hasUI && (mode==="print"||mode==="json")`), enforced at `extensions/loops/goal-activation.ts:1247` (`if (isWorkerSessionCtx(ctx)) return;` before root/restore/owner writes).
- Bounded run reproduces: `bun test` on the 4 cited files → `58 pass, 0 fail` (verified this session).
- Diff is doc-only (survey doc + active.jsonl), consistent with "no port on negative finding".

### Blocking gap: cited "exact test evidence" does not pin the guard
Section 9 correction claims `the guard is pinned by 4 test files` with lines `last-wins:174, stale-self-heal:112, stale-continuation-integration:111, stall-handling:55`. Grep of those files shows:
- `stale-self-heal.test.ts:112` = `SRC.slice(...indexOf("function isForeignCtx"...))` — self-heal ordering assertion, not a worker-admission assertion.
- `stale-continuation-integration.test.ts:111` = a comment (`// Now foreign ctx is different cwd...`).
- `stall-handling.test.ts:55` = `if (isForeignCtx(ctx)) return; noteActivity(true)` — activity gating, not `isWorkerSessionCtx` refusal.
- Only `last-wins.test.ts:174` mentions `isWorkerSessionCtx`, and only for ownership-refresh (`refreshOwnershipStanding`), not `session_start` admission refusal.
- No cited line asserts `goal-activation.ts:1247` refusal. A reader following the citations cannot verify the "no hole" verdict.

The actual direct behavioral pin was omitted: `tests/subagent-host-boundary.test.ts` (4 tests, all pass this session) — `worker cannot be first claimant`, `persistent workers cannot masquerade as silent host successors`, with `workerCtx` (`mode="print"`, `hasUI=false`) refused at `session_start` without mutating state. That is the evidence the verdict needs, and it is uncited.

Secondary: body text still says `Pinned across 7 test files`; the appended correction contradicts it without fixing it.

## Required fixes
- Fix survey §9 body: remove/replace the false `Pinned across 7 test files` sentence so the section is internally consistent.
- Cite the real guard evidence: `tests/subagent-host-boundary.test.ts` (worker-first-claimant, foreign-command, persistent-masquerade tests) with exact test names/lines plus its bounded `bun test` result; keep the 58/0 run only with an accurate characterization (ownership/continuation/stall coverage, not guard pinning) or drop it from the guard claim.
- Re-run and record both bounded runs with exact pass/fail counts after the doc fix.

**Verdict record inspected:** `audit/CROSS-HARNESS-SURVEY-2026-09-11.md` §9 — finding "no hole exists", "Nothing to port; steal-table row 9 closed."

- `extensions/loops/goal-session.ts:1589` — `isHostSuccessorCtx` file-backed structural fallback; `:1849` — `isForeignCtx` (`isWorker || deniedCwd || ownerSession mismatch`), fail-closed.

- `foreignToolGuard` + `claimProcessOwner` gates continuation/tools as cited.

**Behavioral pins verified in test source:**
